findings.evidence: src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_evaluation.py, run_stage_e: "before = prediction_receipt[\"ordinal\"]" and "after = lifecycle.next_ordinal(\"PREDICTION_SEALED\", \"LABELS_OPENED\", before)" derive the ordinal entirely from the supplied receipt; the function returns a result but records no consumed state. src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_lifecycle.py, next_ordinal: "if current_ordinal != 0: raise LifecycleError(...)" only refuses a caller that supplies a nonzero value. src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_evaluation.py, result construction: "\"ordinal\": after" returns rather than persists the advanced ordinal.
findings.reproduction: Obtain any valid lock, prediction receipt, members, labels, and strata accepted by run_stage_e. Invoke run_stage_e once, then invoke it again with byte-identical arguments, including the original receipt whose ordinal remains 0. Each invocation computes after=1 and returns a terminal EVALUATED_ACCEPTED or EVALUATED_NOT_ACCEPTED result; neither invocation is refused as a second formal evaluation.
findings.residual_limitation: Persisting a consumed ordinal must also be paired with an authenticated, create-only terminal-result namespace; it alone does not prove that all runtime inputs were the registered sealed objects.
findings.title: Stage E does not consume the formal evaluation ordinal and can be run repeatedly

findings.evidence: src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_evaluation.py, run_stage_e verifies only "if canonical_digest(list(sealed_members)) != prediction_receipt[\"stream_digest\"]" and then iterates "for member in sealed_members:". It has no assertion that len(sealed_members), prediction_receipt["member_count"], or the scored denominator equals lifecycle.EXPECTED_SET_MEMBER_COUNT. The only missing-label check is "missing = sorted({m[\"case_id\"] for m in sealed_members} - set(labels))", which likewise covers only supplied members. src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_lifecycle.py defines "EXPECTED_SET_MEMBER_COUNT = 120", but run_stage_e does not use it.
findings.reproduction: Create a valid lock and lock digest. Supply sealed_members=[{"case_id":"c1","prediction":{"answer_presence":"present","canonical_value":"x"}}]. Construct a self-consistent receipt with state "PREDICTION_SEALED", ordinal 0, the lock digest, member_count 1, stream_digest=canonical_digest(sealed_members), and receipt_digest=canonical_digest(receipt without receipt_digest). Supply labels={"c1":{"eligible":True,"answer_presence":"present","canonical_value":"x"}} and strata={"c1":"S01"}. run_stage_e accepts the receipt and returns PASS with eligible_case_count 1 because all mismatch counters are zero.
findings.residual_limitation: Checking the count prevents denominator shrinkage but does not by itself authenticate that the members are the cases represented by the preregistered set manifest.
findings.title: Stage E can return PASS for a stream shorter than 120 cases

findings.evidence: src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_evaluation.py, create_preregistration_lock: "if existing_lock_digest is not None: raise EvaluationError(...)" accepts creation whenever its optional caller-supplied existing_lock_digest is omitted, and returns only "frozen, canonical_digest(frozen)" without retaining a lock object or existence record. src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_evaluation.py, seal_prediction_stream declares "existing_objects: Iterable[str] = ()" and passes it to lifecycle.assert_create_only_plan. src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_lifecycle.py, assert_create_only_plan only evaluates "existing = set(existing_objects)" and refuses collisions in that supplied iterable; it neither reads nor retains object existence.
findings.reproduction: Call create_preregistration_lock(bindings=valid_bindings) twice, omitting existing_lock_digest both times; both calls succeed, including if the second bindings differ. Separately, call seal_prediction_stream twice with the same valid stream, sealed_case_ids, write_order, and terminal_manifest while omitting existing_objects; both calls accept because each sees the default empty iterable. These calls can yield fresh receipts/results instead of refusing a second write.
findings.residual_limitation: A persistent create-only store or authenticated append-only ledger is also required to establish that a claimed existing-object listing was complete and was observed before the attempted write.
findings.title: Preregistration and prediction seals are not create-only without caller-provided existence state

findings.evidence: src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_construction.py defines REVIEWER_FORBIDDEN_INPUTS as exact names including "old_label" and "migrated_label". Its asserted enforcement is only "present = sorted(set(packet).intersection(REVIEWER_FORBIDDEN_INPUTS))" in assert_reviewer_packet_is_blind, followed by a check only for "case_content" and "public_ontology_packet". Unlike the Stage P guard, it does not recursively inspect keys or reject unknown fields.
findings.reproduction: Call assert_reviewer_packet_is_blind({"case_content":"case", "public_ontology_packet":{}, "gold_label":"secret"}). The required fields are present and gold_label is not an exact member of REVIEWER_FORBIDDEN_INPUTS, so the packet is accepted and can be handed to a reviewer despite carrying a label-bearing field.
findings.residual_limitation: A field-level guard cannot establish reviewer independence from shared execution context, filesystem, or transcript; those isolation properties require the separately configured runtime boundary.
findings.title: Reviewer blinding admits unregistered label-bearing field names

findings.evidence: src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_lifecycle.py defines STAGE_E_FORBIDDEN_READ_CLASSES including "parser_source" and "parser_invocation". src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_evaluation.py, run_stage_e receives "labels: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]]", assigns "label = labels[case_id]", and reads selected label keys, but has no payload-field rejection for parser-bearing data. Its only parser check is "lifecycle.assert_stage_e_import_is_parser_free(loaded_module_names)", which inspects a caller-supplied sequence of module names rather than the received label payload.
findings.reproduction: Use the one-member otherwise-perfect receipt and inputs described for A-02, but set labels["c1"]["parser_source"]="parser bytes" and pass loaded_module_names=(). run_stage_e reads the label mapping, performs no parser-field check, and returns PASS. Thus parser-bearing material reaches the Stage E role despite its forbidden class.
findings.residual_limitation: Rejecting parser-bearing payload fields does not prove process-level parser absence; the runtime image and module-loading boundary must independently remain parser-free.
findings.title: Stage E accepts parser-bearing fields embedded in its label payload

report.summary: Audited the supplied lifecycle, construction, evaluation, rehearsal tests, and methodology documents for one-shot execution, admission, blinding, bounded repair, sealing, collision rules, and Stage E gates. The construction-side closed vocabularies, deterministic content-hash ordering, collision rules, and scoring-gate recomputation are substantively implemented. However, the formal lifecycle is represented only by caller-supplied values: Stage E can be called repeatedly with the same sealed receipt, and can issue PASS for a one-member stream if supplied a self-consistent forged receipt. Preregistration and prediction create-only checks likewise rely on caller-supplied existence listings rather than retained state. Reviewer blinding has an exact-name blacklist that admits label-bearing variants, and Stage E accepts parser-bearing fields inside labels. These are paths to invalid scientific results or prohibited disclosures.
unverifiable_without_private_material: Whether production storage and entrypoint implementations, not supplied here, persist object existence, consumed ordinals, and create-only writes.
Whether deployed reviewer and arbiter execution environments are actually isolated despite the documented role lanes.
Whether any private set, label, prediction, or deployed result conforms to the public protocol.
